newsitem.title: USA: Permanent Bancorp stake raised by group.
newsitem.headline: Permanent Bancorp stake raised by group.

text.p: A group of Michigan investors, including LaSalle Capital Management Inc, on Monday said it increased its stake in Permanent Bancorp Inc to 142,900 shares, or 6.7 percent, from 121,000 shares, or 5.7 percent.
In a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, the group said it bought 21,700 shares between May 2 and May 16 at $23.25 to $23.625 each.

Separately, the group, which previously disclosed that it plans to seek representation on Permanent's board, proposed a third nominee, Ronald Hollander. The nomination was made in a letter to Permanent, the group said in its SEC filing.
The group last month submitted both Wallace Riley and Robert Lucas as nominees for the company's board.

"The group's purpose in seeking representation on the issuer's board of directors is primarily to attempt to influence the board of directors to consider all possible strategic alternatives available," the LaSalle group said in the SEC filing.
"One way of achieving this goal is to seek out another financial institution and attempt to implement a business combination," the group said in the SEC filing.
Further, the LaSalle group said it wants to influence the company's board "to explore seriously" such a plan, among others, in consultation with independent financial advisers.
